newsitem.title: USA: US home mortgage interest rates fall again in week.
newsitem.headline: US home mortgage interest rates fall again in week.

text.p: The average interest rate for U.S. 30-year fixed-rate mortgages fell to 7.59 percent in the week ending November 15, a fourth consecutive weekly decline, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp said Thursday.
Freddie Mac said this week's rate was the lowest for 30-year mortgages since the week ended March 8, 1996, when the average was 7.38 percent. Last week's 30-year rate was 7.67 percent.
Fifteen-year loans also fell a fourth consecutive week to an average 7.11 percent, the lowest since a rate of 6.87 percent in the March 8 week. Last week's 15-year rate averaged 7.20 percent.
Adjustable rate mortgages inched downward to an average 5.52 percent, the lowest since a rate of 5.40 percent in the week ended March 8. Last week's ARM averaged 5.56 percent.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.35 percent, the 15-year 6.86 percent, and the ARM 5.65 percent.
"With the economy slow but stable, there is little fear of inflation in the market and this is reflected in lower interest rates again this week," Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist, said.
"Indications are good that we may well see interest rates even lower next week," Van Order added.
Earlier Thursday the Labor Department said October consumer prices rose 0.3 percent. On Wednesday the Federal Open Market Committee left interest rates unchanged.
Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average 1.8 percent in fees and points on 30- and 15-year loans, both up from 1.7 percent last week. They charged 1.4 percent on the ARM, unchanged from last week.
